details: Bitcoin surged above $65,000, driven by lower-than-expected U.S. June Consumer Price Index (CPI) data. Headline inflation dropped by 0.4% monthly, bringing the annual rate to 3.5%, and core inflation eased to 2.6%. This cooling inflation reduced fears of aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes, sparking a broader crypto market rally. Notably, BlackRock clients purchased $138.9 million in Bitcoin on July 15, contributing to significant ETF inflows. Despite the rally, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index remains in "extreme fear" at 25, although showing signs of improvement.
title: Bitcoin Reclaims $65K as US Inflation Cools, Boosting Market Sentiment

details: Japan's parliament has approved landmark legislation reclassifying Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies as financial assets. This significant regulatory shift moves digital assets from the country's payments regime to the framework governing traditional financial instruments like stocks and bonds. The move also clears the way for a plan to cut the top tax rate on crypto gains from 55% to a flat 20%, effective from 2028.
title: Japan Reclassifies Crypto as Financial Assets, Approves Tax Cut

details: The U.S. and UK Treasuries have jointly released 10 recommendations aimed at aligning their regulatory approaches for stablecoins, tokenized assets, and capital markets. Developed by the Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future, this initiative seeks to facilitate cross-border blockchain-based finance and has been met with positive reception from industry players like Coinbase.
title: US, UK Propose Joint Roadmap for Stablecoin & Tokenization Rules

details: The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) has commenced its first production trades of tokenized stocks and U.S. Treasuries. This significant development involves participation from major financial institutions including JPMorgan, BlackRock, and Goldman Sachs, signaling a growing integration of digital assets into traditional financial market infrastructure.
title: DTCC Initiates Tokenized Stock & Treasury Trades with Major Banks

details: JPMorgan analysts have highlighted a potential threat to Circle's USDC revenue sharing model due to the increasing dominance of the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid. Hyperliquid now holds approximately $6 billion in USDC, accounting for about 8% of its total supply, creating a "prisoner's dilemma" that pressures the profitability of Circle and Coinbase in their USDC distribution agreements.
title: JPMorgan Warns Hyperliquid Dominance Poses Risk to Circle's USDC Revenue

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has chosen 36 payment companies and banks from across the euro area to participate in a 12-month digital euro pilot program. Among the selected firms are Deutsche Bank, UniCredit, Revolut, and Stripe. Testing for the retail central bank digital currency (CBDC) is scheduled to begin in the latter half of 2027, with a potential issuance slated for 2029, contingent on legislative approval.
title: ECB Selects 36 Firms for Digital Euro Pilot Program

details: The team previously leading the Ethereum Foundation's institutional privacy work has spun out to establish EthSystems, an independent, for-profit company. EthSystems will focus on developing privacy and compliance technology, enabling banks and asset managers to conduct transactions on the Ethereum blockchain while ensuring the confidentiality of sensitive information.
title: EthSystems Launches as For-Profit for Ethereum Institutional Privacy
